utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60/1-S, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, very much. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Peter McCloskey and Stefan Waespi and Janet Stewart for the Prosecution. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the accused Momir Nikolic is myself, Veselin Londrovic, and my co-counsel, Mr. Stephan Kirsch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference. There are two purposes for this Status Conference. The first one is we would like to provide opportunity to Mr. Nikolic. Now, opportunity for him to communicate directly with the Trial Chamber. Secondly, it's for the preparation of the sentencing hearing. May I now turn to Mr. Nikolic first. Mr. Nikolic, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It has been a long time since the last time we saw each other. How about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm in excellent health, Your Honour. I have no health problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any comments concerning your detention in the UN Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The conditions are in accordance with the rules and I find them acceptable. I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any other issues that you would like brought to the attention of this bench?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have discussed all outstanding issues with my lawyers and whatever is to be raised before Your Honours will be done by my counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, we turn to the second issue, that is the preparation for the sentencing hearing. The Prosecution and Defence filed their sentencing briefs on the 14th July 2003. Both parties indicated that they would file additional submissions on Mr. Nikolic's cooperation with the Prosecution, after Mr. Nikolic has testified in the Blagojevic case. At this stage, it seems to us that Mr. Nikolic will be testifying in middle to late September. I have a question to address to the both parties, how much time after he completes his testimony will the parties need to file any additional submissions? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We shouldn't need more than two weeks. We hope to, of course, be busy in trial at that time. Two weeks should be fine for us, but we're very flexible on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Londrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence will not need more than two weeks either for their submissions after Mr. Nikolic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In our view, two weeks is too long. Could we move a little faster. For instance, how about ten days?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask for two weeks, Your Honour, but there is not much difference between ten days and 14 days, and if Your Honour orders us to do this in ten days, we will respect that deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. I understand that Defence has requested that the Trial Chamber requests the commanding officer of Detention Unit to prepare a report on Mr. Nikolic's behaviour in the Detention Unit. Is that right, Mr. Londrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In our written submission, we asked the Chamber to address the head of the Detention Unit, the commanding officer, to prepare a report on Mr. Nikolic's behaviour in the Detention Unit, covering Mr. Nikolic's attitude toward the staff, the employees in the Detention Unit, and his attitude towards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the other accused who are on the same floor with him in the Detention Unit and with whom he socialises and shares his life in the Detention Unit. We talked to Mr. McFadden's deputy and we intended to address them directly, but we were told that the only way we could obtain such a report would be through the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Londrovic, according to the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, the registrar and the Chamber are separate, independent organs of this Tribunal. Usually, the correct approach is that the counsels should exhaust all the means at his proposal to get any assistance from the warden of the Detention Unit. If there is any problem, if it poses some serious problems in the conducting of the proceedings, only at that time the Trial Chamber will lend its assistance and its support. So the best way is you write a letter to the warden of the Detention Unit to see whether you could be helped or not. If not, you are free to come back to the Bench and we'll do our best to assist you. Is that understandable?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I understand. You suggest we apply again to the warden, and if we have any problems, to apply you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, the next issue is about the sentencing hearing. If Mr. Nikolic finishes his testimony by late September, the Trial Chamber would like to schedule the sentencing hearing for late October or earlier November. Are there any obstacles for the parties for holding the sentencing hearing at that time and how long do you think that sentencing hearing will last? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time has no obstacles to that, and the Prosecution's sentencing material will be submitted in written form, as it has been, originally relying on the excellent record and testimony of the Krstic case. So the Prosecution will say a few words at the sentencing hearing and that would be that unless the Court wanted something further from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has absolutely no problems with late October or early November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you think how many days do you need for this sentencing hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence is concerned, Your Honours, the Defence suggested that five witnesses be heard. The examination of these witnesses, if Court approves all five, can be completed within one day. These will be brief testimonies. And if the Bench sits for half a working day, then we would need two days at the most. If you understand my meaning. If we were to sit both in the morning and the afternoon, then we could complete this in one day. I see, however, that the practice at the Tribunal is for one Chamber to sit in the morning and another in the afternoon. And in this case, it would take us two days at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are considering addressing the registrar to get testimonies under Rule 92 bis. If we succeed in this, according to the procedure prescribed in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we are prepared to submit these five testimonies under Rule 92 bis. And in this way, we would avoid hearing the witnesses viva voce and we would be saving money and time in this way. We shall try to contact the registry in order to get these statements under Rule 92 bis before late October, that is early November, and adduce these statements to our submission. In that case, we would have no viva voce witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There are two things I would like to stress at this moment. The first matter is that we will hold separate sentencing hearings for Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Obrenovic, because the case has been separated into two cases. Secondly, I would like to remind the parties that evidence presented at the sentencing hearing should not go to establish a conviction, only for the seriousness of the offense. Victim impact, character of the accused, for aggravating or mitigating circumstances. Well, Mr. Londrovic, of course if you submitted all those five witness's statements according to 92 bis, it's all right, but we believe that the proposed witnesses touches on slightly different aspect of Mr. Nikolic's character and the background, especially the Bosniak witnesses are particularly helpful to the Trial Chamber. And it will help the Trial Chamber to have a better understanding of the impact of the guilty plea on the witness and the victimised community. Of course, you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could choose whatever way to introduce your evidence, but we are ready to hear all the five witnesses, all sum of them in this courtroom. Suppose some of the witnesses are going to testify in the sentencing hearing, I understand the Defence has put in a confidential motion for protective measures on the 14th of July for three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence did require this for three witnesses, three witnesses were ethnic Bosniaks, whereas two witnesses are of Serb ethnicity, so we did not ask for protective measures for them, because they did not require any when speaking to me. They said they didn't want any, while these three witnesses did ask for a pseudonym and for facial distortion. It was my understanding, Your Honour, that you would like the Defence the make an effort to bring in witnesses to testify here, notably ethnic Bosniaks. So we are going to speak to our client about this and we are going to see what we should do on that score. However, we will certainly try to facilitate these proceedings for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. We will try not to bring in all five witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any objections for the protective measures sought by the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if not, we would like to say that your requests for the protective measures for those witnesses, no matter they are the live witness or they are the 92 bis witness, are granted. Can I turn to the Prosecution. Would you please inform me, are there any witnesses, no matter live or 92 bis witnesses, in the sentencing hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We were not planning on any live witnesses, and we just have the few witnesses in our sentencing brief for 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that Defence has not filed any response, but proposals of the Prosecution for these four witnesses. Could I hear the response from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence certainly has no objections to having these witness statements filed, that is to say, the statements that were part of the Pre-Trial brief of the Prosecution. They can be introduced through Rule 92 bis. The Defence does not oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we could like to make a decision to grant the request to have the four witnesses pursuant to 92 bis without the cross-examination by the Defence. Yes. At this stage are there any matters that both parties would like to bring to the attention of this bench. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Londrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the hearing is adjourned. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 3.26 p.m. 25
